ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The $16$ squares on a piece of paper are numbered as shown in the diagram. While lying on a table, the paper is folded in half four times in the following sequence:

fold the top half over the bottom half
fold the bottom half over the top half
fold the right half over the left half
fold the left half over the right half.

Which numbered square is on top after step $4$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a 4-by-4 grid. The top row is numbered 1, 2, 3, 4; the second row is 5, 6, 7, 8; the third row is 9, 10, 11, 12; and the bottom row is 13, 14, 15, 16. Reasoning: Keep each pile ordered from top to bottom. Fold 1, top half over bottom half: row 2 lands on row 3 and row 1 lands on row 4, giving stacks [5,9], [6,10], [7,11], [8,12] in the upper resulting row and [1,13], [2,14], [3,15], [4,16] in the lower resulting row. Fold 2, bottom half over top half: the lower row stacks flip, so the four stacks become [13,1,5,9], [14,2,6,10], [15,3,7,11], [16,4,8,12]. Fold 3, right half over left half: the right two stacks flip and land on the left two stacks; the left resulting stack has 9 as its bottom layer. Fold 4, left half over right half: that left stack flips over, so its former bottom layer becomes the top layer. Therefore the numbered square on top is 9.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a 4-by-4 grid numbered row by row: top row 1,2,3,4; second row 5,6,7,8; third row 9,10,11,12; bottom row 13,14,15,16. Then simulate the folds with stacks, keeping each stack ordered from top to bottom. Rule: when a half is folded over, the moved half lands on top of the stationary half, and the layer order within each moved stack reverses because the stack flips. After fold 1, top half over bottom: each bottom-half cell receives a stack from the reflected top row above it. After fold 2, bottom half over top: reverse and place the lower row stacks over the upper row stacks, giving one row of four stacks, with the leftmost stack top-to-bottom [13,1,5,9]. After fold 3, right half over left: reverse the right-side stacks and place them over the left-side stacks, producing two stacks; the left stack has bottom layer 9. After fold 4, left half over right: reverse the left stack and place it over the right stack, so its former bottom layer becomes the final top. Therefore square 9 is on top.

The last fold is left half over right half, so the final top must be the bottom layer of the left-half stack just before step 4, because that left stack flips.
